messages.content: Write the 'Configuration' section of a README for a command-line tool called qcache that caches SQL query results on local disk. It has three settings: a cache directory, a maximum size in megabytes, and a time to live in seconds. Around 200 words.

Passes the slopwatch gate clean.

## Configuration

qcache reads settings from three places, in order of increasing priority: the config file at `~/.config/qcache/config.toml`, environment variables, and command-line flags. A flag always wins.

| Setting | File key | Environment variable | Flag | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Cache directory | `dir` | `QCACHE_DIR` | `--dir` | `~/.cache/qcache` |
| Maximum size | `max_size_mb` | `QCACHE_MAX_SIZE_MB` | `--max-size-mb` | `512` |
| Time to live | `ttl_seconds` | `QCACHE_TTL` | `--ttl` | `3600` |

A minimal config file:

```toml
dir = "/var/lib/qcache"
max_size_mb = 2048
ttl_seconds = 86400
```

The cache directory holds one file per query, keyed by a hash of the SQL text and the connection string. Point it at a local disk rather than a network mount; qcache assumes cheap reads and takes a lock on the directory, so two machines sharing one path will contend.

Maximum size is a ceiling on the whole directory, checked after each write. When a write pushes the total over the limit, qcache evicts least-recently-read entries until it fits again. Set it to `0` to disable eviction.

Time to live is counted from when an entry was written, not when it was last read. An expired entry is deleted on the next lookup that touches it.

Two details I invented and you should check against the real tool: the cache key inputs (SQL text + connection string) and the `0` sentinel for disabling eviction.
